algorithm.Title: Animal Bite - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Animal or human bite wound assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for uncontrolled bleeding, major tissue injury, face/neck airway threat, shock, reduced consciousness, or a dangerous animal/ongoing threat. Apply continuous direct pressure with a clean dressing unless an object is embedded. Move to safety without attempting to capture the animal. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Was this an insect bite rather than a mammal or human bite or an insect sting?
questions.Information: A non-sting insect bite requires the authored Insect Bite pathway.

questions.Question: Was this a bee, wasp, or yellow-jacket sting rather than a mammal or human bite?
questions.Information: A bee, wasp, or yellow-jacket sting requires the authored Bee or Yellow Jacket Sting pathway.

questions.Question: Is the wound large or deep, or is bleeding not stopping with direct pressure?
questions.Information: NHS.UK animal and human bites guidance lists a large or deep wound, or bleeding that cannot be stopped, as Qatar 999/an emergency assessment service selected through the Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) criteria.

questions.Question: Might there be debris such as teeth, hair, or dirt in the wound; is it hot, swollen, or leaking fluid; is there fever or chills; does it smell unpleasant; is it on the hands, feet, face, or head; was it a human bite; or has the caller not had a tetanus vaccine in the last 10 years?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance lists these as reasons to seek clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) for same-day assessment rather than manage entirely at home.

questions.Question: Is this a minor, shallow bite with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes most bites as not serious and manageable at home with basic first aid.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency bite response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for uncontrolled bleeding, major tissue injury, face/neck airway threat, shock, reduced consciousness, or a dangerous animal/ongoing threat. Apply continuous direct pressure with a clean dressing unless an object is embedded. Move to safety without attempting to capture the animal. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: bleeding will not stop; pale, cold, faint, confused, or unresponsive person; airway, face, hand, genital, tendon, nerve, or major-joint injury.

advice.Title: Urgent bite wound review
Content: Clean the wound with soap and warm water, cover with a clean dressing, and arrange same-day medical review for possible antibiotics or tetanus assessment.
Call Back If: increasing redness or swelling; fever develops.

advice.Title: First aid while arranging bite assessment
Content: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water, pat dry, and cover with a clean dressing; do not squeeze or deliberately make it bleed. Human/animal species, location, depth, rabies exposure, tetanus status, antibiotic need, immunocompromise, pregnancy, and medication choice require prompt in-person assessment under the approved Qatar pathway.
Call Back If: increasing warmth, swelling, redness, pain, pus, red streaks, or fever; loss of movement/feeling or worsening general condition.

references: NHS.UK, "Animal and human bites", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/animal-and-human-bites/ (page last reviewed 27 October 2025)
